verdicts.rewritten_summary: HRW report (26 Mar 2026): India's parliament passed the 2026 Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill narrowing the 2019 law: it removes self-identification, restricts legal recognition to traditionally recognised groups (hijra/kinner) and intersex persons, and requires medical certification for identity recognition — reversing the 2014 Supreme Court ruling. The bill adds offences including up to life imprisonment for 'coercing or alluring' anyone to be transgender, which HRW warns could criminalise support networks. Of 487,803 census-recorded transgender persons, only about 32,500 hold identity cards. HRW urges the president not to sign; assent pending as of late March 2026.

BBC (26 Mar 2026): India's parliament passed an amendment to the 2019 transgender-rights law replacing self-identification with recognition based on biological or physical traits plus traditional identities (hijra/kinner-style); medical boards and district authorities must now certify gender-affirming surgery. The government says the narrower definition targets welfare benefits and anti-trafficking protection; critics warn it excludes many trans men, trans women and non-binary people. A Supreme Court-appointed advisory panel asked the government to withdraw the bill, calling removal of self-identification a setback against the 2014 ruling; presidential assent is pending. India is estimated to have around two million transgender people.
